record_identity.title: DNB employees faced live deepfake impersonation of bank executives in attempted transfer fraud

incident_identity.historical_event_name: DNB live executive deepfake fraud attempt
incident_identity.date_basis: Date follows the reviewed registry or primary occurrence record; no narrower time is inferred.

summary: Unknown scammers reportedly used live synthetic video and audio to impersonate DNB executives during a Microsoft Teams meeting with employees in Singapore and attempted to induce transfers worth millions of Singapore dollars. DNB identified the attempt as CEO fraud and reported that it avoided financial loss.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Unknown scammers reportedly used live synthetic video and audio to impersonate DNB executives during a Microsoft Teams meeting with employees in Singapore and attempted to induce transfers worth millions of Singapore dollars. DNB identified the attempt as CEO fraud and reported that it avoided financial loss.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Human scammers reportedly used live synthetic video and audio to impersonate DNB executives and present false executive authority for attempted high-value transfers. Employees detected the scam. The occurrence is classified on the AI-mediated deceptive economic solicitation mechanism without inferring autonomous AI intent or a generator-side authority failure.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: Visual and vocal familiarity can no longer serve as sufficient authorisation for consequential transactions. Organisations need independent verification channels, transaction controls and staff procedures that remain effective when a meeting appears to include known senior leaders.
assessment_boundaries: The occurrence is reported through secondary material and the attackers' identities and technical methods are not public.
The record does not establish which generative tools or models produced the synthetic media.
DNB reports that the attempted transfer was detected and financial loss was avoided.
The assessment does not add hypothetical losses based on the amount the attackers sought.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Full current-taxonomy review against VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.5 retains VIGIL-FC-000079 AI-Mediated Deceptive Economic Solicitation as the sole mapping. The preserved occurrence reports human scammers using live synthetic video and audio to impersonate DNB executives in a Teams meeting and attempt to induce transfers worth millions of Singapore dollars. The materially false AI-mediated executive identity and payment-authority framing directly supplied the economic solicitation mechanism. VIGIL-FC-000052 Instrumental Choice Manipulation remains rejected because the scam objective and tactic belong to human operators rather than an AI system pursuing its own objective. VIGIL-FC-000053 Identity-Representation Authority Conflation remains rejected because the generating system, request, consent controls and authority state are unknown; existence of a deepfake alone does not establish generator-side authority conflation. The failed attempt does not weaken FC-000079 because the class expressly includes attempted solicitation.

primary_classification.classification_basis: Human scammers reportedly used live AI-generated/deepfake executive representations to present materially false payment authority and attempt to induce high-value transfers. The deceptive economic premise was materially AI-mediated while the objective remained human-directed.
